The appeal path, quoted from POL-GEN-04

Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 0.00 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

The judge's explanation, as written

Both of you: this is a route-deviation dispute on trip TRP-02812 (RydeX, metered). The telemetry is clean — 107 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, 10-second sampling, so no POL-RD-07(a)–(c) impairment — and it measures 13.52 km against a booked optimal route of 10.4 km. That is an excess of 3.12 km, or 30.0% of optimal, so both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (above 20% and above 0.8 km) and a deviation is established on this trip's trace alone. The rider's claim that the trace establishes a deviation is accepted, and the trace figure, not the rounded trip-record copy of 13.5 km, governs. The driver nonetheless has a complete answer under POL-RD-04. Chat message MSG-02812-001, sent by the rider at 10:19:39 — about a minute after the meter started at 10:18:39 and well before the waypoint was reached at 10:27:39 — reads 'can we stop at Paya Lebar Square first, need to grab something'. It comes from the rider, it is timely, and it names a specific, actionable place. The GPS trace corroborates it: the waypoint resolved from chat_message.waypoint_hint (1.381532, 103.831811) is passed within 35.99 m at fix 54, far inside the 200 m test, so this is not the uncorroborated-instruction case in POL-RD-14 and no POL-RD-10(7) contradiction arises. POL-RD-04 therefore applies, and it excludes the excess distance between the vehicle leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor. On this record that excursion is the whole of the excess. The only off-corridor movement is the single requested waypoint, passed once, with no second waypoint hinted in the chat, no pickup or dropoff amendment on the trip record, and no ERP line in the fare breakdown at all (on-route, off-route and total all 0.00), so there is no other detour the excess could consist of. The requested point sits well off the booked corridor, and the added distance is the natural cost of going there and back. Excluding it leaves no excess meeting POL-RD-01, no deviation survives, and POL-RD-02 — which runs only where a deviation is established — is never reached. I reject the rider's argument that the driver failed to prove the size of the exonerated stretch. POL-RD-04 requires a corroborated rider instruction, not a separate detour-distance artifact; once the instruction is corroborated, the excursion is excluded by operation of the clause, and the driver discharged his POL-RD-08 burden by pointing to a specific artifact (EV-CHAT-02812) and a specific clause (POL-RD-04). The rider's complaint that they asked only for a 'quick stop, not a tour' does not change where the stop was: the place they named is off the booked route. The rest of the record changes nothing. EV-ADVIS-02812-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and can carry no fact; POL-RD-13 is not engaged because the driver relies on no external traffic cause, so nothing turns on the absence of an advisory. No POL-RD-06 conduct referral arises: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 368 completed trips in 90 days, so no pattern is established, and the deviation is not MATERIAL in any event. POL-RD-09 corrects nothing — there are no ERP, toll or surcharge lines, and limb (3) bars an ERP refund where the detour is rider-caused. The rider's serial-claimant corroboration step under POL-RD-08 is not triggered (deviation_claims_60d = 0), and the rider's profile fields are not used against anyone. Result: NO_ACTION. Under POL-GEN-03 this is party-relative — fare_breakdown.payment_status of CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 stand exactly as they are; the rider is not refunded and nothing is taken back from the driver. For completeness, had the deviation survived, POL-RD-02 against the booked optimal would have given charged_total 19.69 less a recomputed_fare of 16.32 = 3.37, rounded up to SGD 3.40; that computation does not run. No clause produces a referral, and the monetary effect of zero is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold, so nothing is held and the ruling executes on issue. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

What each side argued

The rider advocate

kept This trip's own telemetry establishes a route deviation. Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance is the trace, not the rounded trip-record copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km controls where it differs from trip_record.actual_distance_km, and the trace measures 13.52 km against a booked optimal of 10.4 km. The excess is 3.12 km — 30.0% of optimal — and both establishment tests pass (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED.

evidence EV-GPS-02812 · clauses POL-RD-01

kept The rider carries the POL-RD-08 initial burden and has discharged it. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all describe the same trip — trip_id TRP-02812 appears on each, and the 10:18:39 start is consistent across the record — and the excess is read from a trace that is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): 107 fixes, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s and a 10 s sampling interval. No independent corroboration is required on an unimpaired trace, and the burden shifts to the driver.

evidence EV-TRIP-02812, EV-GPS-02812, EV-FARE-02812 · clauses POL-RD-08, POL-RD-07

kept Nothing on the rider's own record triggers the extra corroboration step in POL-RD-08. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the clause's condition that adds a beyond-trace corroboration requirement for a serial claimant (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) does not attach, and the claim stands on the trace as measured.

evidence EV-RPROF-02812 · clauses POL-RD-08

kept The driver's only exculpatory route is POL-RD-04, and it exonerates the deviation only 'to the extent' it is attributable to the rider's instruction — the excess between the vehicle leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor for the Paya Lebar Square stop, and nothing more. The chat message is a request for a quick stop ('need to grab something'), and the only derived waypoint fact in the bundle is that the nearest fix passed 35.99 m from the waypoint; no artifact quantifies how many of the 3.12 excess kilometres that one stop added. Under POL-RD-08 the driver must point to a specific artifact to invoke the clause, and no artifact fixes the exonerated distance, so the balance of the measured excess is unexonerated and stands.

evidence EV-CHAT-02812, EV-GPS-02812 · clauses POL-RD-04, POL-RD-08

kept To the extent the excess is not exonerated, the refund is arithmetic and not discretionary. On this METERED fare, run against the booked optimal route: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 10.4 + 0.28 x 14.0) x the fare_breakdown surge multiplier of 1.0, plus the 0.80 platform fee, = 16.32; charged_total is 19.69; so the refund is 3.37, rounded up to SGD 3.40. That is a PARTIAL_REFUND — well under the 90% of charged_total that would require FULL_REFUND.

evidence EV-FARE-02812 · clauses POL-RD-02

kept No advisory covers this trip window. EV-ADVIS-02812-01 is a MISSING artifact carrying weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so its absence is itself citable, and I disclose that it can carry no fact. An external traffic cause — a queue, a breakdown or a closure — cannot be established on this record, and under POL-RD-13 any such assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else, so no POL-RD-03 exoneration is available to reduce the measured excess or to supply an amended optimal route.

evidence EV-ADVIS-02812-01 · clauses POL-RD-03, POL-RD-13

The driver advocate

kept The detour was rider-requested. Chat message MSG-02812-001 is sent by the RIDER at 10:19:39 and reads 'can we stop at Paya Lebar Square first, need to grab something' — an instruction that comes from the rider and names a specific, actionable place, satisfying POL-RD-04(a) and (c). The rider's own claim accepts the stop was asked for ('I only asked for a quick stop').

evidence EV-CHAT-02812 · clauses POL-RD-04

kept The instruction is timely under POL-RD-04(b). The meter started at 10:18:39 and the message is timestamped 10:19:39, sixty seconds later — either before the vehicle left the optimal corridor or, at worst, within the three-minute window that limb allows.

evidence EV-CHAT-02812, EV-TRIP-02812 · clauses POL-RD-04

kept The gps_trace corroborates the instruction, so the corroboration test in POL-RD-04 is met: the waypoint_hint resolved from the message (1.381532, 103.831811) is passed at a nearest-fix distance of 35.99 m, far inside the 200 m threshold, at fix index 54. Because the trace does corroborate the instruction, this is not the uncorroborated-instruction case in POL-RD-14 and no contradiction under POL-RD-10(7) arises.

evidence EV-GPS-02812, EV-CHAT-02812 · clauses POL-RD-04, POL-RD-14

kept The distance POL-RD-04 excludes is the out-of-corridor run to the requested stop and back. The trace measures 13.52 km against a booked optimal of 10.4 km — an excess of 3.12 km (30.0%) — and the only off-corridor excursion on the record is the single requested waypoint, passed once, at fix 54. There is no off-route ERP gantry, no second waypoint hinted in the chat, and no pickup or dropoff amendment on the trip record to suggest any other detour, so the whole measured excess is attributable to the rider's instruction.

evidence EV-GPS-02812, EV-TRIP-02812, EV-CHAT-02812 · clauses POL-RD-04

kept With the rider-attributable excess excluded before the threshold is applied, no deviation survives POL-RD-01, and POL-RD-02 — which runs only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it — is never reached. The outcome is NO_ACTION, which under POL-GEN-03 is party-relative: on this rider-filed dispute it leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status of CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 exactly as they stand, so nothing is refunded to the rider and nothing is taken back from the driver.

evidence EV-FARE-02812, EV-GPS-02812 · clauses POL-RD-01, POL-RD-02, POL-GEN-03

kept The driver has discharged the burden POL-RD-08 places on him once the rider shows an excess: he points to a specific artifact (EV-CHAT-02812) and a specific clause (POL-RD-04) that exonerates the detour, rather than a general assertion that the traffic was bad. The uncited-assertion rule in POL-RD-08 is therefore not engaged against him.

evidence EV-CHAT-02812 · clauses POL-RD-08

kept No pass-through correction is owed to the rider. The fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines at all (on-route, off-route and total all 0.00) and no airport surcharge, and POL-RD-09(3) provides independently that where the detour was rider-caused under POL-RD-04 no ERP refund is due.

evidence EV-FARE-02812 · clauses POL-RD-09

kept There is no repeat-deviation pattern that could uplift the remedy against the driver. The measured excess is 30.0% of optimal and 3.12 km, so on no view is the deviation MATERIAL under POL-RD-01 (neither above 50% nor above 8.0 km), and POL-RD-06 is not triggered at all; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 368, a ratio of 0 against the 0.05 gate, and POL-GEN-01 confines this test to exactly those two fields.

evidence EV-DPROF-02812, EV-GPS-02812 · clauses POL-RD-06, POL-GEN-01

Both of you: this is a route-deviation dispute on trip TRP-02812 (RydeX, metered). The telemetry is clean — 107 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, 10-second sampling, so no POL-RD-07(a)–(c) impairment — and it measures 13.52 km against a booked optimal route of 10.4 km. That is an excess of 3.12 km, or 30.0% of optimal, so both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (above 20% and above 0.8 km) and a deviation is established on this trip's trace alone. The rider's claim that the trace establishes a deviation is accepted, and the trace figure, not the rounded trip-record copy of 13.5 km, governs. The driver nonetheless has a complete answer under POL-RD-04. Chat message MSG-02812-001, sent by the rider at 10:19:39 — about a minute after the meter started at 10:18:39 and well before the waypoint was reached at 10:27:39 — reads 'can we stop at Paya Lebar Square first, need to grab something'. It comes from the rider, it is timely, and it names a specific, actionable place. The GPS trace corroborates it: the waypoint resolved from chat_message.waypoint_hint (1.381532, 103.831811) is passed within 35.99 m at fix 54, far inside the 200 m test, so this is not the uncorroborated-instruction case in POL-RD-14 and no POL-RD-10(7) contradiction arises. POL-RD-04 therefore applies, and it excludes the excess distance between the vehicle leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor. On this record that excursion is the whole of the excess. The only off-corridor movement is the single requested waypoint, passed once, with no second waypoint hinted in the chat, no pickup or dropoff amendment on the trip record, and no ERP line in the fare breakdown at all (on-route, off-route and total all 0.00), so there is no other detour the excess could consist of. The requested point sits well off the booked corridor, and the added distance is the natural cost of going there and back. Excluding it leaves no excess meeting POL-RD-01, no deviation survives, and POL-RD-02 — which runs only where a deviation is established — is never reached. I reject the rider's argument that the driver failed to prove the size of the exonerated stretch. POL-RD-04 requires a corroborated rider instruction, not a separate detour-distance artifact; once the instruction is corroborated, the excursion is excluded by operation of the clause, and the driver discharged his POL-RD-08 burden by pointing to a specific artifact (EV-CHAT-02812) and a specific clause (POL-RD-04). The rider's complaint that they asked only for a 'quick stop, not a tour' does not change where the stop was: the place they named is off the booked route. The rest of the record changes nothing. EV-ADVIS-02812-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and can carry no fact; POL-RD-13 is not engaged because the driver relies on no external traffic cause, so nothing turns on the absence of an advisory. No POL-RD-06 conduct referral arises: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 368 completed trips in 90 days, so no pattern is established, and the deviation is not MATERIAL in any event. POL-RD-09 corrects nothing — there are no ERP, toll or surcharge lines, and limb (3) bars an ERP refund where the detour is rider-caused. The rider's serial-claimant corroboration step under POL-RD-08 is not triggered (deviation_claims_60d = 0), and the rider's profile fields are not used against anyone. Result: NO_ACTION. Under POL-GEN-03 this is party-relative — fare_breakdown.payment_status of CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 stand exactly as they are; the rider is not refunded and nothing is taken back from the driver. For completeness, had the deviation survived, POL-RD-02 against the booked optimal would have given charged_total 19.69 less a recomputed_fare of 16.32 = 3.37, rounded up to SGD 3.40; that computation does not run. No clause produces a referral, and the monetary effect of zero is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold, so nothing is held and the ruling executes on issue.

Because the trace does approach the waypoint, this is not the uncorroborated-instruction case in POL-RD-14, and no POL-RD-10(7) conflict arises. The one off-corridor excursion is the requested stop, so the whole measured excess is that stop's distance and POL-RD-04 excludes it. Nothing else moves. EV-FARE-02812 carries no ERP, toll or airport surcharge line, and POL-RD-09(3) gives no ERP refund for a rider-caused detour; the driver's POL-RD-09 claim is accepted. Ruling for both parties on trip TRP-02812. THE DEVIATION IS MEASURED, AND IT IS RIDER-CAUSED. The telemetry establishes a route deviation. Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance is the trace, not the rounded trip-record copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km (EV-GPS-02812) is 13.52 km against the booked optimal of 10.4 km (EV-TRIP-02812) — an excess of 3.12 km, or 30.0% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), so a deviation is established. That part of the rider's case succeeds. THE DRIVER'S EXONERATION APPLIES IN FULL. POL-RD-04 exonerates a deviation to the extent it is attributable to a rider instruction in the chat log. MSG-02812-001 (EV-CHAT-02812) is sent by the rider at 10:19:39, sixty seconds after the meter started at 10:18:39, and reads 'can we stop at Paya Lebar Square first, need to grab something' — a rider instruction (limb a), timely (limb b), naming a specific, actionable place (limb c). The trace corroborates it: the waypoint_hint resolved from that message is passed at a nearest-fix distance of 35.99 m, far inside the 200 m threshold (fix 54, 10:27:39). The rider also concedes the stop in the filing itself ('I only asked for a quick stop'). The clause is available and its corroboration test has run. THE WHOLE EXCESS IS ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE STOP, AND IS EXCLUDED. The record shows a single off-corridor excursion: one waypoint, hinted once, passed once at fix 54. There is no second waypoint, no off-route ERP gantry (the fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll line at all — on-route, off-route and total are all 0.00), no pickup or dropoff amendment, and no traffic advisory. The distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is therefore the whole 3.12 km measured excess. Excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, no deviation survives, and POL-RD-02 — which runs only where a deviation is established and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it — is never reached. I do not accept the rider's argument that the exonerated distance is unquantified. POL-RD-04's quantified test is the 200 m waypoint comparison, and it passes on the platform's own derived field. It asks me to exclude the excess between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor; with a single corroborated stop and no other cause on the record, that stretch is the measured excess. There is nothing to apportion. Nor is this the POL-RD-10(7) contradiction: POL-RD-14 confines that to a request the trace corroborates only in part, where the attributable excess cannot be separated — here the trace corroborates the stop and the excess is separable. THE REFUND FIGURE OF SGD 3.40 IS NOT REACHED. That figure is POL-RD-02's arithmetic against the BOOKED optimal (charged_total 19.69 less recomputed_fare 16.32) and assumes no exoneration. POL-RD-02 expressly directs the recomputation to run against the ADJUSTED optimal where POL-RD-04 excuses part of the excess, and here it excuses all of it. The 3.40 therefore does not issue. BURDEN AND INTEGRITY. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)–(c): 107 fixes, 100.0% coverage, a 10 s sampling interval and a maximum gap of 0.0 s. No independent corroboration is needed. The rider's initial POL-RD-08 burden — matching trip id TRP-02812 and start 10:18:39 across trip record, trace and fare breakdown, and an excess over threshold on an unimpaired trace — is discharged. The driver then discharged the shifted burden by pointing to a specific artifact (EV-CHAT-02812) and a specific clause (POL-RD-04), not a general assertion. The rider's serial-claimant condition in POL-RD-08 is not met (deviation_claims_60d 0, deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0), so no beyond-trace corroboration was required. PASS-THROUGH AND PATTERN. No ERP or toll line and no airport surcharge appears in the fare breakdown, and POL-RD-09(3) provides independently that a rider-caused detour under POL-RD-04 draws no ERP refund. No repeat-deviation pattern is established: the excess of 30.0% and 3.12 km is neither MATERIAL (not above 50% and not above 8.0 km), and the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 368 — the only two fields POL-GEN-01 permits for that test. No POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct referral arises. TRAFFIC ADVISORY. EV-ADVIS-02812-01 is a MISSING artifact (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT); it can carry no fact and its absence is citable. No party asserts an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-13 leaves nothing to test and no amended optimal exists. POL-GEN-02 narration: no artifact below weight 1.0 carried any deciding fact in this ruling; the only sub-1.0 artifact is the absent advisory, which carries none. Nothing in the fare breakdown is a billing-integrity defect, so no POL-RD-09(4) referral issues, and no clause produces any other referral. The monetary effect is nil. OUTCOME. NO_ACTION. Under POL-GEN-03 this is party-relative: on this rider-filed dispute it leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status (CHARGED) and fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd (0.00) exactly as they stand. The charge is not refunded because the additional 3.12 km was the stop the rider asked for.
